<!-- Source: edit this .qmd, then `quarto render docs/referral_pathways.qmd` → referral_pathways.md.
     GitHub renders the Mermaid blocks natively (no clone / no Pages needed), so every journey is
     viewable on the web even though the repo is private. Generated by pathway_mermaid() — the same
     function as the README teaser, looped over all patients (no hardcoded ids). -->

Static **Mermaid** renderings of every patient's `referral_pathway` — viewable on GitHub without
cloning. For the **interactive** versions (hover / drag / zoom), open
[`../data/out/html/index.html`](../data/out/html/index.html) from a local checkout (they render live
in a browser; GitHub shows them as source). Back to the [README](../README.md).

A revisited phase is one node the journey loops back to; an edge's `xN` label is its traversal count.
*Cyclic* journeys (a phase recurs) are flagged below.

```{python}
# | output: asis
import sys
from pathlib import Path

# find src/ whether Quarto's execute dir is the repo root or docs/
sys.path.insert(0, str(next(p for p in (Path("src"), Path("../src")) if p.exists())))
import post_extraction_eda as eda

records = eda.load_records()
cyclic = {
    r["patient_id"]
    for r in records
    if len(r["referral_pathway"]) != len(set(r["referral_pathway"]))
}
for r in sorted(records, key=lambda r: r["patient_id"]):
    pid = r["patient_id"]
    print(f"### {pid}{' — cyclic (loops)' if pid in cyclic else ''}\n")
    print(eda.pathway_mermaid(records, pid))
    print()
```
